title: Coptisine Improves Liver Inflammation in Sepsis by Regulating STAT1/IRF1/GPX4 Signaling-Mediated Kupffer Cells Ferroptosis.
authors: Zhu, Bingwen; Sun, Chang; Luo, Dongrong; Liang, Yuying; Jiang, Aolin; Jiang, Zehui; Luo, Haihua; Yuan, Gang; Huang, Chenyang; Liu, Shaoqing; Li, Lei; Jiang, Yong
one_liner_zh: 该文研究黄连素改善脓毒症肝损伤中Kupffer细胞铁死亡，涉及STAT1蛋白与DNA结合调控，但核心是药物机制而非TF-DNA互作建模，仅用分子对接辅助，AI/物理模拟方法深度不足。
abstract: Sepsis is a life-threatening condition characterized by organ dysfunction, with the liver being particularly vulnerable due to inflammation triggered by Kupffer cell activation. Ferroptosis, an iron-dependent form of regulated cell death associated with macrophages, has emerged as a key pathogenic mechanism. This study aimed to investigate the protective effects of coptisine (COP), a natural alkaloid, against sepsis-induced hepatic ferroptosis and injury using in vivo and in vitro models. Sepsis was induced in mice via cecal ligation and puncture (CLP) or lipopolysaccharide (LPS) challenge, followed by treatment with COP, ferrostatin-1 (Fer-1, a ferroptosis inhibitor), or 2-NP. In vitro, Kupffer cells were stimulated with LPS + IFN-gamma and erastin to induce inflammation and ferroptosis, then treated with COP or Fer-1. Multiple techniques were employed, including histopathology, enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA), quantitative PCR (qPCR), Western Blot, immunofluorescence (IF), molecular docking, bio-layer interferometry (BLI), and cellular thermal shift assay (CETSA), to evaluate the STAT1/IRF1/GPX4 signaling axis. Additionally, serum markers from sepsis patients were analyzed. In septic mice, COP significantly attenuated liver injury, inflammation, and ferroptosis. In Kupffer cells, COP suppressed erastin-induced ferroptosis. Mechanistically, COP directly bound to STAT1, inhibiting its phosphorylation and subsequent IRF1 activation, while restoring GPX4 expression. Overexpression of STAT1 abolished the protective effects of COP. Clinical data revealed elevated p-STAT1 and IRF1 levels alongside reduced GPX4 in sepsis patients. COP exerts hepatoprotective effects in sepsis by inhibiting ferroptosis through the STAT1/IRF1/GPX4 pathway, highlighting its potential as a therapeutic agent for sepsis-associated liver injury.
abstract_zh: 脓毒症是一种以器官功能障碍为特征的危及生命的疾病，其中肝脏因库普弗细胞（Kupffer cell）激活引发的炎症而尤为脆弱。铁死亡（ferroptosis）是一种与巨噬细胞相关的铁依赖性调节性细胞死亡形式，已成为关键致病机制。本研究旨在利用体内和体外模型，探讨天然生物碱黄连素（coptisine, COP）对脓毒症诱导的肝脏铁死亡和损伤的保护作用。通过盲肠结扎穿刺（CLP）或脂多糖（lipopolysaccharide, LPS）攻击诱导小鼠脓毒症，随后给予COP、ferrostatin-1（Fer-1，一种铁死亡抑制剂）或2-NP处理。体外实验中，用LPS + IFN-γ和erastin刺激库普弗细胞以诱导炎症和铁死亡，然后用COP或Fer-1处理。采用多种技术，包括组织病理学、酶联免疫吸附测定（ELISA）、定量PCR（qPCR）、Western Blot、免疫荧光（IF）、分子对接、生物层干涉法（BLI）和细胞热位移分析（CETSA），评估STAT1/IRF1/GPX4信号轴。此外，分析了脓毒症患者的血清标志物。在脓毒症小鼠中，COP显著减轻了肝损伤、炎症和铁死亡。在库普弗细胞中，COP抑制了erastin诱导的铁死亡。机制上，COP直接结合STAT1，抑制其磷酸化及随后的IRF1激活，同时恢复GPX4表达。STAT1过表达消除了COP的保护作用。临床数据显示，脓毒症患者中p-STAT1和IRF1水平升高，而GPX4水平降低。COP通过STAT1/IRF1/GPX4通路抑制铁死亡，在脓毒症中发挥肝脏保护作用，凸显其作为脓毒症相关肝损伤治疗药物的潜力。
